newsitem.title: CHINA: China begins registration of state assets.
newsitem.headline: China begins registration of state assets.

text.p: All enterprises in China have been required to declare the amount of state assets that they possess or are using from January 1, an official and major newspapers said on Monday.
Enterprises established before January 1, 1997, must register the amount of state assets they own or are using, an official of the State Administration of State Property told Reuters.
Those covered would include state enterprises, stockholding companies, Sino-foreign joint ventures, cooperative ventures and jointly managed firms, newspapers said.
The move was designed to "standardise management of state assets", newspapers said. Theft of state assets has been rampant in recent years.
Registration was due to end on June 30 and those which fail to register would be punished, the official said. He declined to give further details.
A survey conducted by the administration estimated the value of state-owned assets at more than 5.71 trillion yuan ($688 billion) at the end of 1995, newspapers said.
